answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making each identity post stake that is slashed on misbehavior. Each new agent locks a bond of nectar, the network's staking token, in a kernel contract that releases it only after 90 days of audited good conduct. Voting weight grows with the bond and age, not with identity count, so splitting funds across 1,000 fakes buys no extra influence. Attackers also forfeit the bond when caught colluding, and basalt-grade reputation takes months to earn, making mass identity farming costly and slow.
